notes: The two eras conflict. 'saṃvat 1753' (VS) gives about 1696 CE, but 'śāke 1718' gives about 1796 CE, a difference of 100 years. ŚS 1718 matches VS 1853, so 'saṃvat 1753' is probably a slip for 1853. ŚS 1718 is adopted here. Weekday check by my own calculation: 9 July 1796 CE was a Saturday and about 3.5–4 days after the new moon of early July, with the Sun in sidereal Mithuna. That fits Āṣāḍha śukla 4/5 well, but it hasn't been checked against a full pañcāṅga. The VS 1753 alternative (1696 CE) was not checked. The colophon gives the text as a 'praśnavidyā' by Ṛṣiśarmācārya and the section as 'nāmavadhaprakaraṇa'. The catalogue title Jñānālaṅkṛtamañjarī does not appear in the colophon. The author's name could be taken as Ṛṣiśarman; '-śarman' was removed as a suffix. 'Āpā' is a common Marathi personal name, so the scribe may be a Deccani brahmin.
